collection.description: A villager unveils an oddly lovable, badly proportioned statue, and the village decides what to do with it.

intro.name: The statue
intro.text:
(sculptor) unveils a sculpture made from driftwood, volcanic ash, crushed snail shells and several extremely unfortunate-looking pearls. It depicts {SUBJECT}.
Its proportions are dreadful. One eye is enormous. The other seems to be looking toward a different village. The left arm is longer than the entire body. Yet something about the sculpture is oddly lovable.

question.name: The Master Carver
question.text: The Master Carver stares at it for a full minute. "I cannot decide whether to praise you or bury it."

choices.label: Enter it into the sculpture competition.
Ask the villagers what it makes them feel.
Let the artist revise the work.

a1.text: The judges award it low marks for craftsmanship. The villagers, however, adore it and begin leaving flowers at its feet. The organizers establish a separate People's Favorite award.

a4.text: The Master Carver declares it an offense against stone, wood and sight itself. Later, (carver.he/she) is discovered secretly sketching it. "For study," the critic insists. Nobody believes (carver.him/her).

b1.text: Children insist the statue looks friendly. Adults begin to agree. It becomes the village's unofficial good-luck monument.

b2.text: A child bursts into tears upon seeing it at dusk. The sculpture is moved to a sunny spot where it looks considerably less threatening.

b3.text: An elderly villager says the crooked face reminds (elderly.him/her) of a lost friend. The audience falls quiet. The artist decides to keep the flaws exactly as they are.

b4.text: Half the village loves the statue; the other half wants it hidden. The leaders choose a public place where it can be admired without blocking anyone's path. The argument continues for years.

c1.text: (sculptor) corrects the proportions. The sculpture becomes technically excellent and completely forgettable. The villagers beg for the crooked version back.

c2.text: The artist displays the original beside the corrected version. The judges debate which is better. A child says, "That one looks right. This one looks happy." Nobody can improve on the answer.

c3.text: (sculptor) refuses to change a thing. "It is ugly," (sculptor.he/she) admits. "But it is mine." The Master Carver grants a reluctant nod.

a2__fx.text: The sculptor wins. A rival demands to know whether the judges have eyes. The Master Carver replies, "Unfortunately, yes. I shall never forget what I have seen." The award stands after a fair vote.

a2__text.text: The sculptor wins. A rival demands to know whether the judges have eyes. The Master Carver replies, "Unfortunately, yes. I shall never forget what I have seen." The award stands after a fair vote.

a3__fx.text: The elder depicted in the sculpture sees the enormous nose and bursts into laughter. "You have captured my finest feature!" (sculptor) is relieved. The elder requests a second statue for home.
